To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the numerical methods for static problems in vehicle system dynamics are well established, whereas the numerical methods for dynamic problems are still under development.

the numerical methods and software tools for the dynamical analysis of vehicle systems and their components have reached an advanced level of maturity and efficiency that allows to solve a broad range of practical problems in vehicle system dynamics with high reliability and high efficiency.

the dynamical behaviour of engineering systems is governed by a few basic laws of nature, that the mathematical models of engineering systems can be transformed into standard problems of numerical mathematics, that numerical standard methods can be adapted to exploit some specific structures of the mathematical models and that the development of new numerical methods and software for new problem classes is a continuous and challenging task in the future.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of numerical methods that are robust and efficient, that are easy to use for the user of vehicle system dynamics and that are suitable for the analysis and optimisation of complex vehicle systems and vehicle components in the frequency range of practical relevance.
the development of robust and efficient numerical methods for vehicle system dynamics and the implementation of these methods in software tools for vehicle system dynamics.
numerical methods for nonlinear systems of equations and for ODEs or implicit DAEs with semi explicit structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
numerical methods in vehicle system dynamic have been and are still a driving force in numerical mathematics.
the numerical analysis of engineering systems in vehicle system dynamics is today in a very healthy state and that the future is promising.
the numerical methods in vehicle system dynamcis are in a mature stage, but there is still room for further improvements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the numerical methods for vehicle system dynamics are in good shape, but still have a lot of room for further improvement and innovation.
the state of the art methods and software tools for the computer based simulation and optimisation in vehicle system dynamics are today mature and well developed.

the numerical methods for static problems in vehicle system dynamics are well developed and that the numerical methods and tools for dynamical analysis are state of the art, but that there are still some challenges in the development of numerical methods and software for the analysis and simulation of contact, real time capable and multidisciplinary problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
these problems can be tackled by a systematic extension of the existing numerical methods and software.
the numerical simulation of vehicle systems is a very active field and the development of new numerical methods is an ongoing challenge.
these problems may be successfully tackled by a combination of classical numerical methods with modern software techniques.
